clinician.trajectory_summary: A 64-year-old female patient, undergoing immunotherapy with nivolumab and ipilimumab for pleural mesothelioma, presented with a 2-month history of progressive cognitive disturbances (disorientation, inattention, forgetfulness, confusion, visual hallucinations, naming difficulties) and systemic symptoms (asthenia, adynamia, gait instability, heat intolerance, nocturnal sweating, palpitations, tremors, low mood). These symptoms began coinciding with the initiation of immunotherapy. Diagnostic workup revealed elevated total T4 and T3 levels, suppressed TSH, and the presence of anti-thyroglobulin antibodies, while anti-thyroid-stimulating hormone receptor antibodies (TRAb) and anti-thyroid peroxidase (TPO) were absent. It was concluded that the delirium was caused by a thyrotoxicosis episode within the context of autoimmune thyroiditis, secondary to the ICI treatment. Symptomatic treatment with beta-blockers was initiated, leading to a gradual amelioration of neurological manifestations. The patient was discharged with advice to continue her oncological regimen and was scheduled for outpatient endocrinology monitoring.
